questions.question:
Why is the following code problematic (you can assume correct inputs, shapes and arguments)?

      import torch

      class MyModule(torch.nn.Module):
          def __init__(self):
              super().__init__()
              self.conv = torch.nn.Conv2d(...)

              def forward(self, x):
                  out1 = self.conv(x)
                   ... # process "out1" so it can be an input to "linear"
                   linear = torch.nn.Linear(...)
                   out2 = linear(out1)
                   return out2

options.text:
torch.nn.Linear is assigned to a local identifier but torch.nn.Conv2d is not. Both should be defined to locals or the code
                   will suffer from reproducibility.
torch.nn.Linear must be invoked before passing the data to the convolutional layer.
torch.nn.Conv2d can never be combined with torch.nn.Linear.

The submodule torch.nn.Linear is created inside the forward method rather than the __init__ method. This means
                   that the submodule is repeatedly created in every forward call, including its random parameter initialization.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

      import torch

      class MyModule(torch.nn.Module):
          def __init__(self, a):
              super().__init__()
              self.a = a

              def forward(self, x):
                  output = x + self.a
                  return output

      my_module = MyModule(2.0)
      c = my_module(5.0)
      print(c)

options.text: It raises an exception because super().__init__() should not be used with torch.nn.Module.
It raises an exception because the __getitem__ method is missing in MyModule.
It raises an exception at self.a = a because only PyTorch trainable parameters and submodules can be used as attribute.
